extracted.intended_audience: U.S. employers/petitioners, immigration practitioners, and prospective Q-1/Q-2/Q-3 and R-1 nonimmigrant applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and criteria governing USCIS petitions for international cultural exchange visitors (Q-1), Irish peace process cultural and training program visitors and dependents (Q-2/Q-3), and nonimmigrant religious workers (R-1), including eligibility, documentation, petitioning, approval, revocation, employment and stay limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return transportation liability for terminated beneficiaries (P-class context)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an alien enters under section 101(a)(15)(P) and employment terminates for reasons other than voluntary resignation, the employer whose offer formed the basis of the status and the petitioner are jointly and severally liable for the reasonable cost of return transportation abroad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Abroad' means the alien's last place of residence prior to entry into the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission purpose and period for Q-1 international cultural exchange visitors
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonimmigrant may be authorized to enter as a Q-1 participant for the purpose of providing practical training, employment, and sharing the history, culture, and traditions of the alien's country of nationality; the period of admission is the duration of the approved program or 15 months, whichever is shorter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Q-1 admitted under this provision is classifiable as Q-1 status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readmission limitation for Q-1 participants (one-year foreign residency)
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien admitted as a Q-1 may not be readmitted in Q-1 status unless the alien has resided and been physically present outside the United States for the immediate prior year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brief trips to the United States for pleasure or business during the immediate prior year do not break the continuity of the one-year foreign residency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to petition for an international cultural exchange program and participants
rubrics_metrics.description: A U.S. employer must petition the Attorney General on the USCIS-prescribed form for approval of an international cultural exchange program and must simultaneously petition on the same application for authorization of one or more individually identified aliens to be admitted in Q-1 status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility for admission will be considered only if the international cultural exchange program is approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program validity period for Q-1 petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Each petition for an international cultural exchange program is approved for the duration of the program, which may not exceed 15 months, plus 30 days to allow travel arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A new petition must be filed each time the qualified employer wishes to bring in additional cultural visitors; replacements for named participants may be admitted until the petition expiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility to the public requirement for program approval
rubrics_metrics.description: The program must take place in a school, museum, business or other establishment where the American public, or a segment thereof, is exposed to aspects of a foreign culture as part of a structured program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities in a private home or isolated business setting to which the public does not have direct access do not qualify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural component requirement for program approval
rubrics_metrics.description: The program must have a cultural component that is essential and integral to the visitor's employment or training and must be designed to exhibit or explain attitudes, customs, history, heritage, philosophy, or traditions of the visitor's country of nationality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultural component may include seminars, courses, lecture series, or language camps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work component must be integrated with cultural component
rubrics_metrics.description: The visitor's employment or training may not be independent of the cultural component; the work must serve as the vehicle to achieve the cultural objectives so that sharing the visitor's culture results from employment or training with the qualified employer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q-1 visitor eligibility criteria (age, qualifications, communication, prior residency)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible as an international cultural exchange visitor an alien must be at least 18 when petition filed; qualified to perform the service or receive the training stated in the petition; able to communicate effectively about cultural attributes to the American public; and if previously admitted as a Q-1 must have resided and been physically present outside the U.S. for the immediate prior year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer supporting documentation to establish 'qualified employer' status
rubrics_metrics.description: To establish eligibility as a qualified employer, the petitioner must submit evidence that it: (A) maintains an established international cultural exchange program per paragraph (q)(3); (B) has designated a qualified employee representative to administer the program and liaise with INS/USCIS; (C) is actively doing business in the United States; (D) will offer wages and working conditions comparable to local domestic workers similarly employed; and (E) has the financial ability to remunerate participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supporting documentation as prescribed must accompany the petition except when repeating a previously approved program in the same calendar year (copy of initial program approval may substitute).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitioner's certification requirements for Q-1 petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner must give each participant's date of birth, country of nationality, level of education, position title, and a brief job description, verify and certify participants are qualified for the service/training, and report and certify wages and working conditions are comparable to local domestic workers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These certifications must accompany the petition as part of required supporting documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form, fee, and documentation filing requirements for Q-1 petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: A U.S. employer must file a petition on the USCIS-prescribed form, with the applicable fee, and appropriate documentation; a new petition with fee must be filed with the appropriate service center each time the employer wants to bring in additional visitors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Service will request additional documentation only when clarification is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple participants per Q-1 petition and required identifying information
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner may include up to 25 named participants on a petition and must include name, date of birth, nationality, and other identifying information and indicate the U.S. consulate at which each participant will apply for a Q-1 visa (or port of entry for visa-exempt participants).

rubrics_metrics.name: Itinerary requirement for services or training in more than one location
rubrics_metrics.description: If the petition requires the visitor to engage in services, labor, or training in more than one location, the petition must include an itinerary with the dates and locations of services, labor, or training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate petition requirement for services/training from more than one employer
rubrics_metrics.description: If the visitor will perform services or labor for, or receive training from, more than one employer, each employer must file a separate petition; the visitor may work part-time for multiple employers provided each has an approved petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of employer during Q-1 status requires new petition
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Q-1 visitor in the United States decides to change employers, the new employer must file a petition, but the total period the visitor may stay remains limited to fifteen months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitution/replacement of participants without filing a new petition
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner may substitute or replace a person named on a previously approved petition for the remainder of the program without filing a new petition, provided the substitute meets qualification requirements and the petitioner notifies the relevant consular/Service office by letter and includes the approval notice copy and required identifying and certification information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioner must certify wages and working conditions comparable to those accorded to local domestic workers.

rubrics_metrics.name: USCIS director's approval procedures and validity rules for Q-1 petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The director will consider all evidence submitted, may request additional evidence, notify petitioner and consulate(s) of approval, and an approved petition is valid for the length of the approved program or 15 months, whichever is shorter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition shall not be approved for an alien who has an aggregate of 15 months in the U.S. under Q-1 unless the alien has resided and been physically present outside the U.S. for the immediate prior year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial notification and appeal rights for Q-1 petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner shall be notified of denial, reasons for denial, and the right to appeal under part 103; a petition for multiple participants may be denied in whole or in part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition revocation reporting requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner shall immediately notify the appropriate Service center of any changes in the employment of a participant which would affect eligibility under section 101(a)(15)(Q)(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic revocation triggers for Q-1 petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Approval is automatically revoked if the qualifying employer goes out of business, files a written withdrawal of the petition, or terminates the approved program prior to expiration; no further Service action is necessary and automatic revocation may not be appealed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation on notice: grounds and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The director shall send a notice of intent to revoke if he or she finds that (A) the visitor is no longer employed or receiving training as specified, (B) the petition's statement of facts was not true and correct, (C) the petitioner violated terms of the petition, or (D) the Service approved the petition in error; the notice shall contain detailed grounds and allow time (30 days) for rebuttal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petitioner may submit evidence in rebuttal within 30 days; the director will consider all relevant evidence in deciding whether to revoke in whole or in part; partial revocations leave remainder approved with revised approval notice; revocation with notice may be appealed under part 103; automatic revocation may not be appealed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of stay limitation for Q-1 visitors
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien's total period of stay under Q-1 cannot exceed 15 months; authorized stay may be extended within that limit if beneficiary of a new petition filed in accordance with paragraph (q)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A new petition filed by the same employer should include a copy of the previous approval notice and a letter indicating any changed terms and conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment authorization and employer restriction for Q-1 visitors
rubrics_metrics.description: A Q-1 alien may be employed only by the qualified employer through which the alien attained Q-1 status; employment outside the specific program violates the terms of Q-1 status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Q-1 alien is not required to apply for an employment authorization document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wages and working conditions requirement for Q-1 employment
rubrics_metrics.description: Wages and working conditions of an international cultural exchange visitor must be comparable to those accorded to domestic workers similarly employed in the geographical area of employment, and the employer must certify such conditions on the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See paragraph (q)(4)(iii)(B) for certification reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irish Peace Process Cultural & Training Program (Q-2) principal residence requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal alien must have been physically resident in Northern Ireland or specified counties of the Republic of Ireland for at least 3 months immediately preceding application and must show no intention of abandoning this residence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q-2 age eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal alien must be between ages 18 and 35.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q-2 employment/training eligibility pathways
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal alien must either (1) be unemployed for at least 3 months, or have completed/currently be enrolled in certain publicly funded training/employment programs or have been made redundant/received notice of redundancy; or (2) be currently employed and nominated by employer to participate for additional training/job experience benefiting participant and employer upon return.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q-2 program duration and admission limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal intends to come temporarily for not to exceed 36 months for training, employment, and coexistence and conflict resolution experience; no more than 4,000 participants (including spouses & minor children) admitted annually for three consecutive program years beginning FY2000; program expires on October 1, 2005; admissions under certain H provisions reduced by one per Q-2 admission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These caps and expiration are statutory/regulatory limits in effect as stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q-2 initial admission documentation and port restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal and dependents must present valid passports and Q-2 or Q-3 visas; those who received visas at U.S. Embassy Dublin or Consulate Belfast must have initial admission at Pre-Flight Inspection facilities at Shannon or Dublin airports; principal must present a Certification Letter issued by the Department of State's Program Administrator documenting selection; dependents may be asked for relationship documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q-2 brief departure/readmission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal, spouse, and minor children may make brief departures not to exceed 3 consecutive months and be readmitted without a new visa, but such time outside will not be added to the end of stay; departures exceeding 3 consecutive months require reapplication, a new visa, and a Certification Letter before re-admission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q-2 length of stay and extension to 36 months
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal and accompanying/following-to-join spouse/minor children are admitted for the duration of the planned program or 36 months, whichever is shorter; participants admitted for less than 36 months may extend their stay so that total is 36 months provided the extension relates to employment or training certified by DOS Program Administrator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q-2 employment authorization conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Following endorsement of Form I-94 by a Service officer, a principal admitted under Q-2 may work for employers listed on the Certification Letter issued by DOS Program Administrator; accompanying spouse and minor children may not accept employment unless spouse is also designated as a principal and issued a Certification Letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q-2 change of employer procedure and appeal limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal wishing to change employers must request such change through DOS' Program Administrator; Service will review and grant approval only if new employer is approved by DOS and such approval is communicated to the Service; if denied there is no appeal under this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If approved, Form I-94 will be annotated to show the new employer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q-2 prohibition on holding other jobs and consequences of unauthorized employment
rubrics_metrics.description: A Q-2 principal may only engage in employment certified by DOS Program Administrator and approved as endorsed on the Form I-94; holding other jobs or engaging in unauthorized employment violates Q-2 status and section 237(a)(1)(C)(i) of the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q-2 job loss remedy period
rubrics_metrics.description: A principal who loses employment has 30 days from last date of employment to locate appropriate employment or training, have the job offer certified by DOS Program Administrator and approved by the Service; failure to find appropriate employment within 30 days requires departure of the principal and any accompanying family.

rubrics_metrics.name: R-1 religious worker basic eligibility requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To be approved for temporary admission, an alien must (i) be a member of a religious denomination having a bona fide non-profit religious organization in the U.S. for at least two years immediately preceding application; (ii) be coming to work at least part-time (average at least 20 hours/week); (iii) be coming solely as a minister or to perform a religious vocation or occupation as defined; (iv) be coming at the request of the petitioner to work for the petitioner; and (v) not work in any other capacity except as provided in paragraph (r)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These apply for initial admission, extension, and maintenance of status, up to five years.

rubrics_metrics.name: R-1 ability to work for multiple qualifying employers
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien may work for more than one qualifying employer provided each qualifying employer submits a petition plus all additional required documentation as prescribed by USCIS regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: bona fide non-profit religious organization (R-1 context)
rubrics_metrics.description: Means a religious organization exempt from taxation as described in section 501(c)(3) and possessing a currently valid IRS determination letter confirming such exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: bona fide affiliated organization
rubrics_metrics.description: An organization closely associated with the religious denomination which is exempt from taxation as described in section 501(c)(3) and possessing a currently valid IRS determination letter confirming such exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denominational membership requirement for R-1 petitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: Denominational membership means membership during at least the two-year period immediately preceding the filing date of the petition, in the same type of religious denomination as the U.S. religious organization where the alien will work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minister definition and duties criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: A minister is an individual fully authorized by a religious denomination and fully trained according to the denomination's standards to conduct religious worship and perform duties of clergy; is not a lay preacher; performs activities with a rational relationship to the religious calling; and works solely as a minister in the U.S., which may include administrative duties incidental to ministerial duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: petition, religious denomination, religious occupation, religious vocation, religious worker
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulation defines 'petition' (form and supporting evidence), 'religious denomination' (common creed, worship, doctrine, services, places of worship, or comparable indicia), 'religious occupation' (duties primarily relate to traditional religious function and inculcating creed; not primarily administrative/support), 'religious vocation' (formal lifetime commitment through vows/investitures), and 'religious worker' (individual engaged in and qualified for a religious occupation or vocation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Religious study/training alone does not constitute a religious occupation, though study incident to status is permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: R-1 admission/change-of-status time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: An eligible alien may be admitted or changed to R-1 status for an initial period of up to 30 months from date of initial admission; if visa-exempt, the alien must present original documentation of the petition approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: R-2 dependents (spouse and children) rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Spouse and unmarried children under 21 may accompany or follow-to-join subject to: (A) R-2 status granted for same period/time limits as principal; (B) neither spouse nor children may accept employment while in R-2 status; and (C) primary purpose must be to join or accompany the principal R-1 alien.

rubrics_metrics.name: R-1 extension/readmission and maximum aggregate stay
rubrics_metrics.description: An R-1 alien maintaining status or seeking readmission may be granted extension/readmission for the validity period of the petition, up to 30 months, provided total time in R-1 status does not exceed 5 years; the Petition for a Nonimmigrant Worker to extend must be filed by the employer with required supplement, fee, and supporting evidence per form instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: R-1 five-year maximum stay and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien who has spent five years in R-1 status may not receive an extension and must depart; exceptions: seasonal or intermittent employment or aggregate six months or less per year, or residents abroad who regularly commute for part-time employment, if both petitioner and alien provide clear and convincing proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable proof includes arrival/departure records, transcripts of processed income tax returns, and records of employment abroad.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing jurisdiction and procedures for R-1 petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: An employer seeking to employ a religious worker shall file a petition in accordance with applicable form instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attestation requirements by prospective R-1 employer
rubrics_metrics.description: An authorized official must complete, sign, date an attestation and specifically attest to: (i) that employer is a bona fide non-profit religious organization or bona fide affiliated organization exempt from taxation; (ii) that alien has been a member of the denomination at least two years and is otherwise qualified; (iii) number of members of the organization; (iv) number of employees at the location and summary of their responsibilities (USCIS may request list of employees/titles/duties); (v) number of aliens holding special immigrant/nonimmigrant religious worker status currently or within past 5 years employed by organization; (vi) number of special immigrant/nonimmigrant religious worker petitions/applications filed by/on behalf of any aliens for employment by the organization in the past 5 years; (vii) title of position offered and detailed daily duties; (viii) whether compensation is salaried or non-salaried and details of compensation; (ix) that alien will be employed at least 20 hours/week; (x) specific location(s) of proposed employment; and (xi) that the alien will not be engaged in secular employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS may request additional employee lists and details at its discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required evidence relating to petitioning organization for R-1 petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition shall include: (i) a currently valid IRS determination letter showing tax-exempt status; or (ii) for organizations recognized under group tax-exemption, a currently valid determination letter establishing group tax-exempt status; or (iii) for bona fide affiliated organizations granted tax-exempt status as something other than a religious organization, a currently valid determination letter establishing tax-exempt status plus documentation establishing the religious nature and purpose (organizing instrument, organizational literature, and a religious denomination certification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation must establish the religious nature and purpose of the organization as prescribed.
